title: Grade 4 CREATIVE ARTS — Premium Revision Paper #8

pages.quiz:
CREATIVE ARTS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #8
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why do we collect only dead or fallen twigs? (1 mark)
   A. Because they are heavier
   B. Because they are wet
   C. Because they are green
   D. To protect the environment and living trees

2. If you tighten the skin of a drum, the sound becomes (1 mark)
   A. softer for ever
   B. lower
   C. silent
   D. higher

3. Which pieces should be pasted first in a montage? (1 mark)
   A. The back pieces
   B. The front pieces
   C. The title only
   D. The smallest pieces

4. After painting, how should you store a brush? (1 mark)
   A. Under a heavy book
   B. Standing on its hairs in water
   C. Washed and laid flat or with hairs upwards
   D. Covered in paint

5. Why is colour classification useful in painting? (1 mark)
   A. It tells us which colours to mix to make others
   B. It makes paint cheaper
   C. It makes paper thicker
   D. It cleans the brush

6. Which is the first step in mixing green? (1 mark)
   A. Use only white
   B. Put yellow and blue on the palette
   C. Put red and black on the palette
   D. Use only water

7. Where can you get pictures for a montage? (1 mark)
   A. Only from the bank
   B. Old newspapers and magazines
   C. From a rock
   D. From the sky

8. A value scale strip shows (1 mark)
   A. only black paint
   B. a picture of a mountain
   C. only primary colours
   D. steps from light to dark of one colour

9. Repeating a small group of notes in a rhythm helps listeners to (1 mark)
   A. change the words
   B. forget the pattern
   C. stop listening
   D. remember the pattern

10. Free hand lettering means writing letters (1 mark)
   A. with a printing machine
   B. with a ruler only
   C. in capital letters only
   D. by hand without a ruler or stencil

11. The home note of the melodies in this lesson is (1 mark)
   A. none of them
   B. m
   C. d
   D. r

12. The middle note of d, r and m is (1 mark)
   A. none
   B. r
   C. m
   D. d

13. In the worked melody of this lesson, the last note is (1 mark)
   A. d, a crotchet
   B. m, a quaver
   C. r, a rest
   D. a pair of quavers

14. Variation in a melody means using (1 mark)
   A. different syllables and note lengths
   B. no rhythm
   C. only one syllable
   D. only rests

15. On the Kenyan flag, green stands for (1 mark)
   A. the rivers only
   B. the land and natural wealth
   C. the sun
   D. the people

16. Which is a sprint distance in big athletics competitions? (1 mark)
   A. Half marathon
   B. Marathon
   C. 100 metres
   D. 10 000 metres

17. In an elongated start, the rear knee is level with (1 mark)
   A. the toes of the front foot
   B. the front knee
   C. the start line
   D. the heel of the front foot

18. In a good sprinting technique, the elbows are bent to about (1 mark)
   A. a straight line
   B. a right angle
   C. a full circle
   D. a tiny angle

19. Why do we warm up before gymnastics? (1 mark)
   A. To make the mat softer
   B. To learn songs
   C. To make us tired
   D. To prepare the muscles and joints

20. A song about washing hands to prevent germs is a (1 mark)
   A. topical song
   B. funeral song
   C. naming song
   D. marriage song

21. Which is good singing posture? (1 mark)
   A. Slouching
   B. Bending over
   C. Standing tall with shoulders relaxed
   D. Hiding behind others

22. Call and response in a folk song means (1 mark)
   A. everyone is silent
   B. a single hum
   C. a soloist leads and the group answers
   D. two drums only

23. Why use a camera strap? (1 mark)
   A. To keep it wet
   B. So the camera does not drop
   C. To cover the lens
   D. To make it heavy

24. When photographing a child, it is good to (1 mark)
   A. shout
   B. photograph from above only
   C. bend down to their eye level
   D. stand on a chair

25. The bottom part of the recorder is the (1 mark)
   A. beak
   B. thumb hole
   C. foot joint
   D. head joint

26. A descant recorder is made of (1 mark)
   A. plastic or wood
   B. glass
   C. metal foil only
   D. paper only

27. Why keep a recorder away from strong sun and fire? (1 mark)
   A. Heat can bend it
   B. It becomes lighter
   C. It becomes invisible
   D. The sun makes it sing

28. In bubble blowing, you blow bubbles (1 mark)
   A. with soap
   B. slowly in the water
   C. on land only
   D. before you enter

29. Outside the pool, in a river or the sea, you should (1 mark)
   A. only go in with a trusted adult who can swim
   B. go in at night
   C. swim alone
   D. dive from rocks

30. How does the hawk tag? (1 mark)
   A. By tripping
   B. By pulling clothes
   C. Gently on the back or shoulders
   D. By pushing

31. In the frog jump, you begin (1 mark)
   A. sitting
   B. in a squat with your hands on the ground
   C. standing on one leg
   D. lying flat

32. The crab walk is done (1 mark)
   A. face down on the tummy
   B. lying still
   C. standing tall
   D. on hands and feet with the tummy facing up

33. The elephant walk is done by (1 mark)
   A. jumping high
   B. bending forward and letting your arms hang like a trunk
   C. running
   D. crawling

34. Animal games improve (1 mark)
   A. only reading
   B. only singing
   C. only cooking
   D. fitness and health

35. In the hawk and the chicks game, the chicks (1 mark)
   A. sing
   B. hold on gently behind the hen
   C. run away
   D. hit the hawk

36. In the hawk and the chicks game, the hen (1 mark)
   A. tags everyone
   B. sits down
   C. protects the chicks
   D. chases the hawk away for ever

37. The Kenya National Anthem is a (1 mark)
   A. a work song
   B. a game
   C. national symbol
   D. a topical song about washing

38. Good feedback should be (1 mark)
   A. kind, honest, specific and helpful
   B. rude and short
   C. only praise with no reasons
   D. only criticism

39. In a folk song, the chorus (1 mark)
   A. conducts the umpire
   B. answers and repeats
   C. paints
   D. hides

40. Which are instrumentalists in a folk song? (1 mark)
   A. The umpire
   B. People playing drums or shakers
   C. The audience
   D. Dancers only

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Give three safety measures to observe when playing netball. (3 marks)

42. Name two parts of a drum. (2 marks)

43. Give four safety rules for sprint races. (4 marks)

44. Describe a sequence that joins the crab balance and the side roll, and how to perform it safely. (5 marks)

45. State four rules of netball. (4 marks)

46. State the lengths of a crotchet rest and a quaver rest and how to show a rest when clapping. (3 marks)

47. Why does a recorder squeak when you blow too hard? (2 marks)

48. State three points of good sprinting technique. (3 marks)

49. Describe the steps of taking a photograph with a digital device. (5 marks)

50. Describe how to compose, write and perform an original four-beat rhythmic pattern. (5 marks)

51. How should clay models be dried and why? (2 marks)

52. Explain why only the Goal Shooter and Goal Attack can score goals. (3 marks)

53. What is a false start? (2 marks)

54. What are ascenders and descenders in lettering? Give one example of each. (3 marks)

55. Describe the roles of the soloist, the chorus and the instrumentalists in a folk song. (3 marks)

56. What are the sol-fa syllables for the three notes learned, and which is the lowest? (2 marks)

57. Why do we get up slowly after a side roll? (3 marks)

58. Give three ways of storing and handling a recorder safely. (3 marks)

59. Why do we play water games in shallow water with the teacher? (3 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #8 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — To protect the environment and living trees
   Cutting living trees harms the environment.

2. D — higher
   A tighter skin vibrates faster and gives a higher sound.

3. A — The back pieces
   You paste the back ones first and then those in front.

4. C — Washed and laid flat or with hairs upwards
   Washing and shaping the tip keeps the brush in good shape.

5. A — It tells us which colours to mix to make others
   Knowing primary and secondary colours helps us mix what we need.

6. B — Put yellow and blue on the palette
   Green comes from yellow and blue.

7. B — Old newspapers and magazines
   Cut pictures from old papers and magazines.

8. D — steps from light to dark of one colour
   A scale strip shows one colour changing from light to dark.

9. D — remember the pattern
   Repetition gives shape and makes the rhythm easier to remember.

10. D — by hand without a ruler or stencil
   Free hand means using only your hand.

11. C — d
   Melodies feel finished when they end on d.

12. B — r
   Ray lies between doh and me.

13. A — d, a crotchet
   The final note is d, on a crotchet.

14. A — different syllables and note lengths
   Variation makes a tune interesting.

15. B — the land and natural wealth
   Green stands for the land and its natural wealth.

16. C — 100 metres
   The sprints are 100 m, 200 m and 400 m.

17. D — the heel of the front foot
   The elongated start puts the knee further back, by the heel of the front foot.

18. B — a right angle
   Bent arms swinging back and forth help the stride.

19. D — To prepare the muscles and joints
   A warm body is less likely to be injured.

20. A — topical song
   It gives a message about a topic of importance.

21. C — Standing tall with shoulders relaxed
   Good posture helps breathing.

22. C — a soloist leads and the group answers
   The soloist calls and the chorus answers.

23. B — So the camera does not drop
   A strap protects the device from falls.

24. C — bend down to their eye level
   Eye level gives a friendly picture.

25. C — foot joint
   The foot joint ends in the bell.

26. A — plastic or wood
   Recorders are commonly made of plastic or wood.

27. A — Heat can bend it
   Heat can warp or crack the instrument.

28. B — slowly in the water
   You put your mouth in the water and blow out slowly.

29. A — only go in with a trusted adult who can swim
   Open water is more dangerous.

30. C — Gently on the back or shoulders
   Gentle tagging keeps everyone safe.

31. B — in a squat with your hands on the ground
   You squat and spring forward.

32. D — on hands and feet with the tummy facing up
   It is like the crab balance, but moving.

33. B — bending forward and letting your arms hang like a trunk
   Slow heavy steps with arms as a trunk.

34. D — fitness and health
   They strengthen muscles and improve stamina.

35. B — hold on gently behind the hen
   Chicks stay in line.

36. C — protects the chicks
   The hen blocks the hawk.

37. C — national symbol
   Like the flag, it stands for the nation.

38. A — kind, honest, specific and helpful
   Good feedback helps the person improve.

39. B — answers and repeats
   The chorus responds to the soloist.

40. B — People playing drums or shakers
   Instrumentalists play instruments.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Remove jewellery, cut long nails, warm up, wear proper shoes, play on flat ground. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each measure.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: Drumhead (skin) and shell (body). Rope and beater are also accepted.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct part.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: Run in your own lane; check the track for stones; wear proper clothes; never push or trip; slow down gradually after the finish; warm up. Any four.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

44. (5 marks)
   Answer: Warm up and use a mat with a clear space. Do a crab balance and hold for three counts. Lower to the mat and lie straight with arms overhead. Do a side roll in a straight line. Get up slowly and finish standing tall.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for safety, crab balance, lowering, roll, and finish.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: No running with the ball; pass or shoot within three seconds; no contact; defenders stand 0.9 metres away; start with a centre pass. Any four.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: A crotchet rest is one beat of silence and a quaver rest is half a beat of silence. When clapping, we do not clap but keep the beat silently.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each length, 1 mark for showing the rest.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: The air is blown too strongly, so the note jumps to a very high shrill sound. Blow more gently.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: Eyes look ahead; elbows bent and arms swing back and forth; knees lift high; land on the front of the foot; body leans forward slightly. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

49. (5 marks)
   Answer: Check the battery and memory and wipe the lens. Decide the subject. Check the light and centre of interest. Hold with two hands and keep elbows close. Frame the subject and press the button gently. Check the result and retake if needed.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid stage.

50. (5 marks)
   Answer: Choose four beats. Fill each with a crotchet, a pair of quavers or a rest. Make sure the pattern has variation and ends on a crotchet. Write it with rhythm names and note symbols. Clap it to a steady beat and improve it after feedback.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for choosing beats, using different values, ending on a long note, writing it and performing it.

51. (2 marks)
   Answer: Slowly in the shade. Strong sun dries them too fast and makes them crack.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: Netball rules say only these two attackers may shoot, and only from inside the goal circle. Other players help by passing the ball to them.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the two players, 1 mark for the goal circle, 1 mark for the role of the others.

53. (2 marks)
   Answer: Leaving the start line before the last signal is given.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for leaving early, 1 mark for before the signal.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: An ascender is the part of a letter that goes up above the small letters, such as b. A descender goes below the baseline, such as p.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning, 1 mark for correct examples.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: The soloist leads, the chorus answers and repeats, the instrumentalists play instruments to keep the beat.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each role.

56. (2 marks)
   Answer: d, r and m. d is the lowest.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for naming, 1 mark for the lowest.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: Getting up fast can make you feel dizzy and you may fall. Slowly is safer.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for dizziness, 1 mark for falling, 1 mark for safety.

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: Keep it in a bag or case; keep away from heat; do not drop it; twist joints gently; do not bite it. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

59. (3 marks)
   Answer: To feel safe and in control, to learn to breathe and move with confidence and to avoid accidents.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.
